A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaskEmbed research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite reformatting and added appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision-probing experiments, CLIPSelf comparisons, VLM benchmark results and extensive appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds loss-function ablations, masked-image-modeling comparisons and ImageNet classification experiments.

M1.justification: The standard MaskEmbed objective, encoder-decoder design and VLM adapter remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 adds an experimentally tested extension that performs feature-reconstruction masked image modeling before or between alignment stages. This extension is explicitly excluded from the other experiments.

E1.justification: New Appendix C evaluates IN1k image classification, extending task coverage beyond COCO probing and the retained VLM benchmarks. ImageNet was already used for alignment training in v1; its classification evaluation is the new coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 6 compares alignment against an in-house CLIP ViT-B masked-image-modeling comparator and sequential MIM/alignment variants. The existing CLIPSelf, pretrained-backbone, adapter and DINOv2-fusion comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces 50-epoch end-to-end IN1k fine-tuning with a transformer classification head and top-1 accuracy, a distinct protocol from frozen-backbone probing. Appendix B.4 adds staged MIM comparisons using five-epoch IN21k fine-tuning. Existing probing and VLM evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 briefly states that cosine and MSE losses behave similarly. v2 expands this into Table 4(d), comparing cosine, L1 and MSE losses and reconstruction of all, masked-only or unmasked-only patches. New Appendix B.4 also tests teacher preparation and alternating MIM/alignment stages. Earlier ablations and case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both present point estimates. Standard deviations used for radar-axis scaling describe variation across models, not experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerical results in Tables 4(d), 6 and 7. Table 7 reports baseline/aligned IN1k accuracies of 82.6/83.1 for CLIP ViT-B, 85.9/86.3 for ViT-L and 86.4/87.0 for ViT-L at 336px. Table 6 newly reports MIM/Align local/global probing scores of 47.30/53.63. Existing Tables 1 and 5 and the main VLM results in Figure 5 retain their values.

T1.justification: Equations (1) and (2), the mask-distribution definition, and the appendix reasoning about feature attribution and objective degeneracy are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and discussion retain the claims of inexpensive self-supervised locality alignment, improved local representations and better VLM performance. The added experiments support these existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains why reconstructing every patch remains useful, interprets MIM as teacher preparation, and discusses the local/global trade-offs of alternating stages. Appendix C adds explanations for improved classification transfer. The existing limitations concerning VLM architecture and training scope remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the additional MIM reconstruction target, five IN21k epochs and reuse of alignment hyperparameters. It also specifies the classification experiment's transformer head, 50-epoch budget and OpenCLIP-inspired settings. Existing implementation tables, hardware disclosures and repository links are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A sharpens the contrast with distillation from other strong models. Appendix B.4 positions feature-based MIM as complementary preparation for alignment and connects this to FLIP-style patch dropping. The bibliography and principal related-work comparisons are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain stable, with localized wording edits and clarifications. v2 adds Appendix B.4 and a classification appendix, shifting the former Appendices C and D to D and E and updating cross-references.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICLR typography, margins, headings and running headers, producing extensive reflow and rescaling. Table 4 gains a loss-function panel, Tables 6 and 7 are added, and Figure 12 changes from side-by-side to vertically stacked panels. New Figure 14 redisplays the existing DINOv2-fusion comparison as radar charts.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through explicit loss ablations, a direct investigation of teacher masking, and IN1k classification after end-to-end fine-tuning across three CLIP backbones. These address questions that v1 treated briefly or supported only through COCO probing. The MIM study also makes local/global trade-offs explicit. These are useful, targeted gains while the main VLM evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
